section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section aimed to investigate the moderating role of ambivalence over emotional expression on the relationship between gratitude and well-being in a sample of Taiwanese students. Across two studies, the results indicated that ambivalence inhibited the relationship between gratitude and subjective happiness. However, this inhibited effect was not supported for the relationship between gratitude and illbeing indexes (loneliness and depression), as these relationships were stronger for high ambivalence.
